answer: A reputation bond resists fake identities: each agent stakes a small refundable deposit before it can trade, and peers can slash it when they catch misbehaviour. Creating many fake identities then costs real value per identity, while honest agents get their stake back. Like a comet that flares once and fades, a cheap fake cannot sustain itself; like quartz, the bond is hard to forge yet easy to verify; and a zephyr of new accounts cannot flood a market where every newcomer must pay to enter. Attack cost scales with the attack.
